Feedback lifetime and closing the dialog

html:
Task deletion and cleanup feedback flows

Deletion has three distinct observations: the browser sent a request, the server accepted removal, and the collector finished cleanup. Task deletion retires a logical task while preserving its conversation and siblings. Conversation deletion uses the conversation lifecycle for selection and durable acceptance. Both clients share the cleanup observer described here.

Task preview, retirement and acceptance

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Task delete control participant API as Conversation routes participant Tasks as TaskDeletionService participant State as Runtime transaction participant GC as Collector and deletion journal UI->>API: POST task delete-preview API->>Tasks: Inspect conversation/task ownership Tasks-->>UI: Identity digest and current work facts UI->>API: DELETE task with selection_digest API->>Tasks: Accept removal alt Attached idle collector Tasks->>GC: Serialize acceptance and find existing owner Tasks->>State: Inspect task and owned request/run scopes State->>GC: Persist intent before publishing retirement GC-->>State: Durable deletion identity State->>State: Retire IDs, fence late writes and update history revision State-->>Tasks: Commit retirement and cancellation identities Tasks->>GC: Reuse collection and wake cleanup Tasks-->>UI: accepted true, deleted false, exclusions and gc UI->>UI: Remove accepted task/request rows immediately UI->>GC: Observe cleanup through status API else No attached collector Tasks->>State: Synchronous deletion transaction State-->>Tasks: Committed result Tasks-->>UI: Deleted task/request identities end Note over State,GC: Runtime transaction and journal are separate owners

task_deletion.js captures the current conversation and task when the user activates Delete task. It disables duplicate actions for that pair, requests a preview, then submits the returned digest. There is no second task confirmation dialog in this helper. The routes delegate to TaskDeletionService.

The preview digest binds delete-task, conversation ID and task ID. It does not freeze the preview's attempt list or reserve execution state. The service checks ownership and discovers the task's current requests, run aliases and applicable continuations when accepting deletion. A continuation bound to a different task does not join that scope. Invalid digests and ownership mismatches cannot authorize another task's removal.

With an attached collector, acceptance holds its acceptance lock and uses the runtime transaction to retire presentation and execution admission. Its intent callback writes the task collection before retirement is published. Journal I/O and the runtime transaction do not form one rollbackable filesystem/database transaction. The durable marker enables replay after restoring an older checkpoint; repeated acceptance reuses the collection's recorded scope and identity. The collector owns deferred payload and saved-copy cleanup, as described in state and recovery.

Retirement records deleted task/request identities, fences owned scratch scopes, retires attempts and pending steering/preparations, updates dependent admission and increments the conversation's history revision. Deferred cleanup avoids rewriting all payload history during acceptance. The synchronous fallback instead performs its deletion in the RAM or attached SQLite transaction available to that service. Cancellation signals and best-effort change notifications follow the decision; they do not prove an external operation stopped. Shared audit evidence retains its own lifetime. The conversation and other tasks remain usable.

The browser unions returned deleted IDs into per-conversation exclusion sets and retains the greatest observed history revision. Late history cannot remove those exclusions. Desktop and mobile callbacks remove matching mounted/provisional turns and refresh their selected view. A response for another conversation does not replace the current selection. Focus moves only when the original focused control has disappeared, focus is on the document body and the same conversation is still selected; a newer draft keeps focus.

After applying exclusions, the helper imports shared cleanup feedback and tracks the returned collection. A failure in that follow-up import can report an error after acceptance already took effect. It does not roll back retirement. The pending-action guard is released and a still-mounted button is re-enabled in the request's finally path.

One observer for cleanup collections

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Desktop or mobile client participant Observer as Shared deletion observer participant API as Collection summary API participant GC as Collector participant View as Rows, feedback and notices Caller->>Observer: begin IDs before conversation request Observer->>View: Fence pending local identities Caller->>Observer: Settle accepted IDs and collection records Observer->>View: Hide accepted identities and announce new owners loop While queued owners remain Observer->>API: One no-store GET with five-second timeout API->>GC: Project compact collection summary alt Status received GC-->>Observer: Current collection states and phases Observer->>Observer: Merge owners and confirmed completion else Read fails or times out Observer->>Observer: Keep fences and mark known owners unavailable end Observer->>View: Dispatch local deletion update Observer->>Observer: Schedule next read after one second end Note over Observer,API: Overlapping triggers share the read owner Note over Observer,View: Notice dismissal does not cancel observation

deletion_progress.js owns page-local pending request reference counts, accepted identity-to-collection mappings, observed collection records and completed identities. Its isDeleted predicate includes accepted queued removal; isComplete requires a completed record or a legacy deleted result. blocked also includes unacknowledged local requests. These are UI fences; server ownership remains authoritative.

begin returns a settlement callback that runs once. It applies only accepted or deleted identities returned by that request and releases its pending reference counts. Settling a request with no result clears those local request counts; it does not establish that an unknown server outcome was rolled back. Later reads, summary ingestion and reload recovery establish what the server accepted.

The observer reads /api/agent/conversation-gc, not one endpoint per row. It polls once at module startup, responds to chats.changed and sync.required, and schedules periodic reads only while queued owners remain. A trigger during an in-flight read requests another pass under the same owner. Conversation summaries can supply gc records directly. Task-only or otherwise unknown noncomplete collections use a synthetic cleanup:<deletion_id> identity. Automatic conversation-purge records also carry conversation identities, including confirmed completion.

A successful read updates known owners present in the summary. A missing record is not interpreted as completion. A failed read marks known collections unavailable and displays Reconnecting without lifting their fences. Once a particular collection has been observed complete, an older incomplete record for that same collection cannot regress it. A new collection is a distinct owner.

Server phases distinguish queued, paused for active tasks, cleaning RAM, waiting for save, purging saved copies, retrying and complete. The browser displays those facts; elapsed time never advances the collector. Background notices count distinct collection owners and appear when a newly observed owner joins the queue. Repeated phase updates do not reopen a dismissed or expired notice.

Feedback lifetime and closing the dialog

flowchart TD Start[Start request feedback] --> Busy[Indeterminate bar and elapsed request time] Busy --> Accepted[Accepted response] Accepted --> Pending[Stop elapsed clock and show observed cleanup phase] Pending --> Complete[All accepted identities confirmed complete] Busy --> Legacy[Legacy deleted response with cleanup or refresh qualifier] Legacy --> Terminal[Complete presentation for committed deletion] Busy --> Error[Unconfirmed request error] Error --> Failed[Failed feedback with retry or review message] Busy --> Close[Close persistent dialog] Close --> Tray[Detached feedback in body tray] Pending --> Tray Complete --> Tray Terminal --> Tray Failed -->|If the dialog closes| Tray Tray --> Expiry[Nonactive result expires after six seconds] Expiry --> Dispose[Remove view, timers and listeners] Observe[Global collection observer] --> Pending Dispose -.-> Independent[Observation and server cleanup remain independent]

create(host) owns one live status region, an accessible progress bar and the elapsed-time display. start begins an indeterminate request; only explicit complete presentation sets aria-valuenow to 1. Request elapsed time uses the monotonic browser clock and is neither a percentage nor a cleanup estimate.

Desktop conversation management and mobile history start persistent feedback before submitting deletion. Desktop Close dismisses the dialog and moves active feedback into a shared tray without aborting the request. After acceptance, the view stops its request clock and follows server phases. An accepted result in the tray can expire after six seconds while cleanup is still pending; the shared observer continues independently.

The legacy deleted_count response uses complete presentation for committed deletion, with any queued/running/retrying storage-cleanup qualifier still shown. That visual state is not a claim that deferred disk work is complete. A subsequent list-refresh failure likewise leaves the committed result intact and adds a refresh hint. A request error before a confirmed result permits retry or another selection review; it cannot establish rollback of a response that was lost.

hide stops the elapsed timer but keeps the view's object and listeners available. dispose removes the view's timers/listeners and an empty tray. Visibility changes only expose presentation state; neither closing nor disposing feedback cancels the server collection or the global observer.

Observed task auto-purge deadlines

flowchart TD Server[Server task retention<br/>and current work policy] --> Snapshot[Selected conversation<br/>snapshot] Viewport[Up to 100 visible task IDs] --> Request[Snapshot request<br/>with observe_task_id] Request --> Snapshot Snapshot --> Observed[Server observed_at<br/>and per-task expires_at] Observed --> Merge[Merge nonolder observations<br/>by conversation] Snapshot --> Policy[Observed policy or pin change] Policy --> Clear[Clear cached deadline entries] Clear --> Merge Merge --> Clock[Deadline minus server observation<br/>minus local elapsed time] Clock --> Labels[Purging in minutes or hours<br/>with retention/protection hint] Labels --> Refresh[Visible countdown refresh<br/>every thirty seconds] Scroll[Scroll debounce<br/>or tab becomes visible] --> Request Refresh --> Request Labels -.-> Zero[Zero is display only] Server --> Eligibility[Server rechecks eligibility<br/>and accepts deletion] Eligibility --> Observer[Deleted IDs and<br/>shared cleanup observation]

The selected snapshot owner passes visible task IDs as bounded observe_task_id parameters. SMTOTaskDeletion.visibleTaskIds selects at most 100 distinct task groups whose vertical rectangles intersect the viewport. The deletion helper caches per-task deadline observations by conversation, rejects older observations, and clears the deadline cache when the observed policy/pin signature changes.

Labels subtract monotonic local elapsed time from the server's observed remaining duration. A missing or null deadline hides the label. Saved retention and unfinished or dependent work appear in its explanatory title. While a visible mounted view has countdowns, a thirty-second timer repaints and requests another selected snapshot. Scrolling debounces a refresh by 200 milliseconds when cached purge data exists; becoming visible also refreshes. These listeners belong to the page-lifetime helper; it exposes no destroy method.

Reaching zero never sends a delete request or removes a task locally. The server owns eligibility, protection, retirement and cleanup. For saved policies, pinning, resume behavior and the difference between task and conversation expiry, use the task auto-purge guide.

Verification boundaries

Task deletion fixtures exercise RAM/SQLite identity ownership, sibling preservation, late writes, continuations, cancellation and retained evidence. Asynchronous task fixtures exercise accepted retirement before payload cleanup, older-checkpoint recovery and yielding collection. Browser fixtures cover deletion feedback and observed task expiry. These are isolated fixtures, not proof of a remote cancellation or a guaranteed wall-clock cleanup deadline. Current test results and retained failures belong in the documentation review status.
